output.summary: KEP-5073 proposes declaring Kubernetes native API validation rules as IDL tags (e.g. +k8s:optional, +k8s:minimum) in types.go files, generated into Go validation code by a new validation-gen tool. Status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Hand-written API validation is hard for users to access, review, maintain, and test, so the KEP moves validation into a declarative IDL framework to reduce technical debt. Migration is intended to be reversible, and the KEP keeps error field and reason stable for clients. Reviewers asked for a runtime mismatch check (DeclarativeValidationMismatchMetrics) so that differences between hand-written and declarative results are detected in the field before the old code is removed.

alternatives.why_not: The readme says hand-written rules are hard to access, review, maintain, and test, which is the problem the KEP targets.

alternatives.option: Run only declarative validation once converted, without a mismatch check
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers wanted the hand-written logic kept running for comparison; deads2k said 'If we stop running the handwritten-we're-trying-to-replace I don't see how we'll detect some classes of declarative validation bugs.'

alternatives.option: Add a separate tag for optional non-pointer fields
alternatives.why_not: thockin said 'I don't think we need another tag. Optional + pointer is obvious.' and analysed the non-pointer case using existing tags.

alternatives.option: Convert the request version instead of the internal hub type before running declarative validation
alternatives.why_not: The consensus was option 2 (convert back to request version before declarative validation), since conversion is cheap and this keeps the changes behind a feature gate.

evidence.quote: Kubernetes API validation rules are currently written by hand, which makes them difficult for users to access directly, review, maintain, and test.
The declarative validation IDL tags will be used to generate code via a new code generator - `validation-gen`.
The KEP has been updated to include a new feature gate - `DeclarativeValidationMismatchMetrics` which controls enabling a code path for runtime validation checks.
If we stop running the handwritten-we're-trying-to-replace I don't see how we'll detect some classes of declarative validation bugs.
since the feature is staying in Beta (it reached beta in 1.33)
